Defining products

Source: vignettes/defining-products.Rmd
defining-products.Rmd

Product order in products() sets cutting priority. Product fields set the trees and log sections eligible for each output.

## Select example trees
trees <- example_trees %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)

## Define export specifications
export <- product(product = 'export',  ## product name, unitless
                  spcd = c(202, 263),  ## species codes, unitless
                  min_dbh = 12,  ## inches
                  min_length = 32,  ## feet
                  max_length = 40,  ## feet
                  trim = 1,  ## feet
                  min_sed = 12,  ## inches
                  inside_bark = TRUE,  ## logical, unitless
                  volume_unit = 'scribner',  ## board feet
                  split_scale = FALSE)  ## logical, unitless

## Define domestic saw specifications
domestic_saw <- product(product = 'domestic_saw',  ## product name, unitless
                        spcd = c(202, 263),  ## species codes, unitless
                        min_dbh = 10,  ## inches
                        min_length = 16,  ## feet
                        max_length = 40,  ## feet
                        trim = 1,  ## feet
                        min_sed = 6,  ## inches
                        inside_bark = TRUE,  ## logical, unitless
                        volume_unit = 'scribner',  ## board feet
                        split_scale = FALSE)  ## logical, unitless

## Define pulp specifications
pulp <- product(product = 'pulp',  ## product name, unitless
                spcd = c(202, 263),  ## species codes, unitless
                min_dbh = 5,  ## inches
                min_length = 8,  ## feet
                max_length = 40,  ## feet
                trim = 0.5,  ## feet
                min_sed = 3,  ## inches
                inside_bark = TRUE,  ## logical, unitless
                volume_unit = 'green_ton')  ## green short tons

## Combine products in cutting priority order
specifications <- products(export = export,
                           domestic_saw = domestic_saw,
                           pulp = pulp)

## Cut and scale the trees
result <- merchandise(tree_id = trees$tree,
                      dbh = trees$dbh,
                      ht = trees$ht,
                      spcd = trees$spcd,
                      products = specifications,
                      model = trees$model)
tree_id log product length (feet) sed (inches) scale (Scribner board feet)

3 1 domestic_saw 40 8.830 120

Tree and log limits

min_dbh and max_dbh apply to tree diameter. min_age and max_age apply to supplied tree age. Lower limits are inclusive. Upper tree diameter and age limits are exclusive.

Missing age prevents eligibility for products with age limits.

min_length and max_length bound candidate nominal lengths. Candidates use the internal half foot grid. min_sed, max_sed, min_led, and max_led constrain physical end diameters. max_logs limits product counts within each segment.

requires_pruned requires the entire cut below pruned_ht. max_sweep rejects overlaps above its percentage limit.

## Define clear specifications
clear <- product(product = 'clear',  ## product name, unitless
                 min_age = 35,  ## years
                 max_age = 70,  ## years
                 requires_pruned = TRUE,  ## logical, unitless
                 min_length = 16,  ## feet
                 max_length = 16,  ## feet
                 min_sed = 6,  ## inches
                 max_sweep = 10,  ## percent
                 volume_unit = 'cubic')  ## cubic feet

## Cut and scale the trees
clear_result <- merchandise(tree_id = trees$tree,
                            dbh = trees$dbh,
                            ht = trees$ht,
                            spcd = trees$spcd,
                            products = clear,
                            model = trees$model,
                            age = 45,
                            pruned_ht = 34)
tree_id log product length (feet) sed (inches) scale (cubic feet)
1 1 clear 16 9.023 9.551
1 2 clear 16 6.227 5.224
2 1 clear 16 11.446 14.262
2 2 clear 16 8.650 9.034
3 1 clear 16 12.581 17.215

age and pruned_ht supply scenario measurements. Southern stands compares explicit age limits across the shipped stand ages.

Cords

cord_solid_fraction supplies the solid wood proportion for the stacked cord conversion.

## Define cordwood specifications
cordwood <- product(product = 'cordwood',  ## product name, unitless
                    min_length = 8,  ## feet
                    max_length = 16,  ## feet
                    min_sed = 3,  ## inches
                    inside_bark = TRUE,  ## logical, unitless
                    volume_unit = 'cord',  ## cords
                    cord_solid_fraction = 0.7)  ## solid wood proportion, unitless

## Cut and scale the trees
cord_result <- merchandise(tree_id = trees$tree,
                           dbh = trees$dbh,
                           ht = trees$ht,
                           spcd = trees$spcd,
                           products = cordwood,
                           model = trees$model)

Prices and validation

price is the amount per price_per volume units. Omitting price leaves the product unpriced and omits log values. Prices and bucking shows priced specifications.

## Check the product table
checked <- validate_products(x = specifications)

## Count validated products
nrow(checked)
#> [1] 3

Source rule conversion

products_from_nvel_rules() translates explicit source rule limits into products, a stump height, and model auxiliaries. Continuous length bounds replace source top segment policies. Factor scaling cannot be translated.

## Specify the source rule fields to translate
rules <- nvel_rules(even_or_odd = 1,
                    option = 14,
                    maximum_length = 32,
                    minimum_length = 16,
                    primary_top = 6,
                    secondary_top = 3,
                    stump = 1,
                    trim = 0.5,
                    minimum_board_foot_dbh = 6,
                    scribner = 'table')

## Translate the rule record
translated <- products_from_nvel_rules(x = rules)

## Inspect the translated result structure
names(translated)
#> [1] "products"  "stump_ht"  "model_aux"
